processing_steps.type: mechanical processing (mechanical alloying / high-energy ball milling)
processing_steps.method: mechanical alloying in a planetary ball mill
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Planetary ball mill (Model no. PM 400/2, Retsch) at 200 rpm; ball-to-powder ratio 10:1; carried out in tungsten carbide (WC) vials with WC balls; toluene used as a process control reagent to avoid oxidation; milling stopped intermittently for 20 min after every 1 h to avoid overheating; 2-3 g of milled powder sampled after every 5 h (so a 15 h aliquot exists) to follow phase evolution.

structures.overall_structure: As-milled powder of the Fe40Mn19Ni15Al15Si10C1 HES after 15 h of milling. The XRD pattern (Fig. 1(a)) is still dominated by diffraction peaks of the constituent elements, and the intensity of the Al peak diminishes after 15 h of milling, indicating that Al has the highest alloying rate. The BCC and γ-brass-type solid-solution phases are not yet formed (they appear only after 25 h of milling), so this 15 h state is a partially alloyed (elemental) powder mixture.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: EMPYREAN, PANALYTICAL diffractometer with Co-Kα source (operating voltage 40 kV; operating current 40 mA); scan rate 5° min⁻¹
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Milled powder at various milling times; patterns recorded at 0, 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30 and 35 h (the 15 h pattern is part of this series)
characterization_methods.purpose: To study the alloying behavior and phase evolution of the powder during mechanical milling
characterization_methods.key_findings: The diffraction peak intensity of all elements decreases with milling time; low-intensity peaks of all elements vanish after 5 h of milling; the intensity of the Al peak diminishes after 15 h of milling, indicating Al has the highest alloying rate; the BCC and γ-brass-type solid-solution phases form only after 25 h of milling.

unmapped_findings: The 15 h milled powder is only an intermediate milling state of the study: full Rietveld-refinement parameters (lattice parameter, phase fraction, crystallite size, microstrain, dislocation density) are reported only for the 25 h, 30 h and 35 h milled powders (Table 2), so no quantitative microstructural parameters are available for the 15 h sample specifically.
Among the constituent elements, Al shows the highest alloying rate during mechanical milling, evidenced by the diminishing intensity of the Al diffraction peaks after 15 h of milling.

No mechanical or physical property measurements were performed on the 15 h milled powder; all reported mechanical properties (microhardness 7.8 ± 0.3 GPa, elastic modulus 184 ± 5 GPa, compressive strength 2046 ± 160 MPa, ~19% compressive strain) and the density (6.49 ± 0.3 g/cc) belong to the spark-plasma-sintered pellet, not to this milling-state sample.
